abandon: The board already contradicts the mechanism. The mechanism says that when the cued base misses a problem it solves in its other samples, the wrong sample started on a working line of attack, wrote a switch phrase, and ended on a later wrong line. It also says RL's gain comes from switching less. (1) result-afc423 judged exactly those samples: "Base items with a right sibling: 39 of 48 slip/misread/format". Wrong plan, the only label a switch to a wrong line would produce, is the minority, and it is concentrated where the base never succeeds: "without (base 0/4): 8 of 12 wrong plan". The error also comes early, not after a first attempt: "First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer." (2) knowledge-1a0674 finds no abandoned right first attempt: "the cued base overwrites a right first answer: 0 of its v3-wrong MATH-500 answers have a right first marker." (3) result-faf15a finds that RL's advantage is not in the choice of line: "RL lowers misreadings and slips, not wrong plans." It gives the per-label numbers "By label for Math 3.1: misread -1.52, slip -0.72, wrong plan +0.03", so RL does not avoid the wrong-plan steps the mechanism says switching causes. (4) result-5e17a6 hand-labelled the 65 RL-only problems: only "2 reached gold then changed it" (plus 9 wrong method and 2 drift), against 14 misread, 14 arithmetic/algebra slip and 16 cap hits. Taken together, the base's misses on problems it can solve are within-line slips and misreadings that RL lowers. They are not working lines abandoned after a switch phrase, so a switch-token penalty has no failure mode to act on.
